title: Send a mimi-content §5.10 session part, for a genuinely external conference URL
description:
Split out of bead mimid-1wgh.114.1 on 2026-11-23, when that bead stopped
being about §5.10 at all.

WHAT §5.10 IS FOR, in its own words: "Joining a conference via an
external URL is possible. The link could be rendered to the user,
requiring a click. Alternatively the URL could be in an ExternalPart with
a disposition of session, which could be processed differently by the
client." The worked example is https://example.com/join/12345.

So the correct use is: somebody has an external conference -- a Jitsi, a
Meet, a SIP bridge -- and wants to put its URL in a MIMI room. That is a
real feature and a real interoperation story with implementations that do
calls that way. It is NOT the keyed call of draft-atwood-mimi-calls, and
it inherits none of its properties: whatever sits behind the URL is not
keyed by any MLS group, and a user must not be led to think it is.

WHAT EXISTS: the receive side, completely. mimid-agent-store content.rs
turns a §5.10 session part into a Call record (url, description, expires,
and is_link, which is true only for https or wss in plain ASCII), the
front ends render it (docs/design/agent-frontends.md §7.24), and
mimid-agent-core tests/session_parts.rs covers it.

WHAT IS MISSING: sending one. There is no Session disposition anywhere in
action.rs or convert.rs.

SCOPE: a Store action that sends a session part, and the front-end paths
to call it. The URL is the CALLER'S: mimid runs no conference service and
must not name someone else's in a message it composes. The limits are
already in content.rs (MAX_CALL_URL_LEN, MAX_CALL_DESCRIPTION_CHARS,
MAX_CALLS_PER_MESSAGE).

P3 deliberately: it is the interoperation half, not the feature. The
keyed call is beads mimid-1wgh.114.1 and mimid-1wgh.114.2.
notes:
THIS BEAD WAS WRONG AND IS CLOSED AS ALREADY BUILT, 2026-11-23, found
when Mark asked what an IRC or live-stream user does about a call.

WHAT I WROTE: "WHAT IS MISSING: sending one. There is no Session
disposition anywhere in action.rs or convert.rs."

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, all of it:
- mimid-agent-core agent.rs Agent::send_session_link builds the §5.10
  session part as an ExternalPart with the join URI;
- mimid-agent-store action.rs:977 Store::send_call is the action, and it
  refuses a URL that is not an https or wss link (Call::is_link) with
  ActionError::InvalidCall;
- mimid-agent-irc service.rs:631 is the `call #channel url
  [description]` command (docs/design/agent-frontends.md §7.24);
- mimid-agent-irc render.rs:558 shows an arriving call as its own ACTION
  line.

MY ERROR: I grepped action.rs and convert.rs for "Session" and reported
the absence as a finding. The action is named send_call and the part is
built in agent.rs, so the grep missed it. A negative result from one
grep over two files is not proof that a feature is absent -- the same
mistake as the dig incident (memory empty-output-is-not-a-finding),
which is about proving a command ran, and this is its sibling: proving a
search looked where the thing would be.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE DESIGN, and it is the useful part:
- IRC ALREADY HAS VTC, of the link kind. An IRC user pastes a conference
  URL, the channel sees it, they click it in a browser.
- The KEYED call cannot reach IRC and must not pretend to. A stock IRC
  client has no media stack, so there is nothing to hand a media secret
  to, and an IRC /call that hosted a parent-dependent room would make a
  room nobody on IRC could join with media. The right IRC behaviour for
  a keyed call started elsewhere is a notice that it is happening and
  that this client cannot join it. Filed as follow-up work.
- THE LIVE STREAM IS A BINDING, NOT A FRONT END (mimid-live; decision
  mimid-1wgh.80). Agent::send_call_signal goes through
  send_content_with to Provider::send, which is the enum over Jmap and
  Stream, so signalling and the media secret ride the live stream
  unchanged. There is nothing to do for it.
- SO decision mimid-1wgh.114's "both routes" has a second reason I had
  not recorded: the link route is not only cross-provider reach, it is
  the only route a front end with NO MEDIA STACK can use, which is both
  of mimid's non-JMAP front ends.
close_reason: Already built: Agent::send_session_link, Store::send_call, the IRC call command and its rendering. The bead rested on a negative grep that looked in the wrong two files.
